samples.summary: Scope bundling: three independent concerns in one change. The stated theme (per the design-doc edit and the new formatter helpers) is unifying the CLI error envelope, but the diff also adds URL path-segment hardening (`seg()`, rejecting `.`/`..`, encoding every id) and re-routes the `api-keys` management calls onto `requestUrl` so they get JWT refresh. Only the error work is reflected in `docs/design/cli.md`. These are separately reviewable and separately revertable; the path-traversal fix in particular is a security change riding along in an error-formatting PR.

The new hard-failure mode introduced by `seg()` is not recorded in the design doc. `HttpClient` now throws `Invalid path segment: ".."` (a plain `Error`, so it surfaces as code `ERROR`) for a document/tab/cell/workspace id of `.` or `..`, and silently percent-encodes every other id. §10's Error Matrix — which this same PR rewrites in detail, down to 80/500/4000-character bounds — has no row for it, and §3/§8 say nothing about id encoding. The PR documents its error contract meticulously while leaving the one new agent-visible failure it introduces undocumented.
searchedFor: grep 'Invalid path segment' across docs/ and packages/cli

samples.summary: §9 still specifies the CLI's own error envelope as `{"error":{"code":…,"message":…,"command":"docs.content"}}`, but no CLI path emits a `command` field (`outputError`, `upstreamErrorJson` and `safeEnvelope` never add one), and the §10 text this PR adds treats `command` purely as an *upstream* sibling field that gets dropped past 4 KB. The PR rewrites the adjacent error contract but leaves §9 asserting a field the contract no longer includes.

The Error Matrix still prints Exit `2` for the `YORKIE_ERROR` and `FONT_LOAD_ERROR` rows while §8.1 (rewritten here) states 2 is never emitted and the footnote says the same. A reader scanning the table gets the wrong answer; the rows should carry the shipped exit code (or be moved into a clearly-separate 'planned' table) rather than being corrected by a dagger.

`HTTP_ERROR` / `SESSION_EXPIRED` are now the universal codes for any backend failure on *every* command, but only the two import skill files document any error codes at all. Per §11 ('self-describing' — skills are the agent-facing contract), the skills for `docs content`, `sheets cells …`, `files …`, `api-keys …` etc. should list the codes agents can now expect; otherwise the newly-unified contract is only discoverable from the design doc.

The README's Design section (adjacent to the Errors/Exit-codes text this work updates) links to `/docs/design/rest-api-and-cli.md` and `/docs/design/docs-cli.md`; neither exists — the canonical docs are `docs/design/cli.md` and `docs/design/rest-api.md`. Nothing in CI checks README links, so this stays broken. Pre-existing, but the same paragraph block is what this change is updating.

`forwardUpstreamError` and `upstreamErrorJson` are two exported helpers with the same classification rule and two different delivery mechanisms (throw-into-`catch` + `console.error` vs. return-a-string), which the doc comments then have to promise produce identical output. A single classifier returning the envelope object, with two thin adapters, would remove the duplicated contract prose and the throw-as-control-flow that requires every call site to sit inside a `try`.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `seg()` at packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:71-76 throws a plain `Error("Invalid path segment: \"..\"")` for a `.`/`..` id and silently percent-encodes all others; it is applied to the workspace (line 108) and to document ids (proven reachable by packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:554-557, `deleteDocument('..')`). Commands pass argv ids straight through with no earlier validation (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:117-248), and formatter.ts has no id guard, so this is a genuinely new, agent-visible failure with no stable code. I searched for documentation of it in: docs/design/cli.md §9 (1035-1047) and the rewritten §10 Error Matrix plus bounds table (1049-1097) — every row covers other conditions, none covers id encoding or dot segments; a repo-wide grep of docs/ for segment|encodeURI|percent-encod|dot segment|traversal; packages/cli/README.md (error-code list at line 118 names only INVALID_DOCX/TYPE_MISMATCH/CONFIRMATION_REQ); and all 19 packages/cli/skills/*.md. The only related text anywhere is the task todo docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:70-73, which states the traversal acceptance criterion but neither the hard-fail nor its code, and which is a task file, not a design doc under docs/design/. No counterexample exists. Blocking under this lens: the PR's own contract goal is that the code an agent branches on is uniform and documented (cli.md:1078-1080), and it documents that contract down to 80/500/4000-char bounds while omitting the one new failure it introduces — an error-contract/design-doc gap, not taste.

finding.summary: `safeEnvelope` breaks the issue's "forwarded verbatim" acceptance criterion (and the doc row that says "(forwarded)") by rewriting the upstream envelope
finding.evidence: `docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:61` states the acceptance criterion: "A backend-shaped body (e.g. TYPE_MISMATCH, SESSION_EXPIRED) is still forwarded verbatim, exit code 1, from *every* command". The plan (lines 21-51) asks only for a shape guard (`isErrorEnvelope`) that forwards the documented envelope or throws `UpstreamHttpError`. The implementation adds an unrequested sanitizing layer on the forward path: `code` truncated to 80 chars (formatter.ts:162), `message` truncated to 500 chars with an ellipsis (formatter.ts:123-125), a `message` starting with `<` replaced by `HTTP <status>` (formatter.ts:122, 165), and all sibling fields (e.g. the documented `command` field on `ApiError`) dropped once the serialized body exceeds 4000 bytes (formatter.ts:167-170). Consequently the design-doc row it added — `docs/design/cli.md:1042` "Backend error body *is* the envelope | 1 | (forwarded) | (the upstream's own code …)" — describes behavior the code does not implement for large or HTML-bearing envelopes. Either the criterion should be renegotiated in the todo/design doc, or the caps dropped; as it stands the shipped pass-through is not verbatim and is not what any spec text describes.

verdict.reason: The finding rests on quoted spec text that is not in the repository. (a) The acceptance criterion at docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:61-69 does not say "forwarded verbatim"; it says the body "still reaches stderr with the upstream's own code, exit code 1, from every command" and then explicitly: "Forwarding is bounded rather than byte-for-byte: the code is never rewritten, but the surrounding text is capped (code 80 chars, message 500 chars, an HTML message replaced by HTTP <status>, sibling fields dropped past 4 KB), because a forwarded body is upstream-controlled content printed into an agent's stderr. Documented in packages/cli/README.md and docs/design/cli.md section 10." That enumerates precisely the four behaviors the reviewer calls unrequested sanitization, and safeEnvelope implements exactly those (formatter.ts:90, 94, 106, 113-126, 158-171) while never rewriting the code value itself (formatter.ts:162-163). (b) The design-doc row is not "(forwarded)" — docs/design/cli.md:1065 reads "(forwarded, bounded)", and lines 1082-1097 add a "Forwarding is bounded, not byte-for-byte" paragraph plus a per-field bounds table naming safeEnvelope and packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts, one row per cap. (c) packages/cli/README.md:129-138 documents the same four caps and adds "Treat message as a display string, not a parseable payload." The reviewer's own proposed remedy (renegotiate the criterion in the todo/design doc) is already satisfied in all three documents the criterion names, so there is no spec/implementation divergence to block on.
